sourceChecks.claim: Reusable copies reduce repeated source work while consuming storage and requiring population.
Application checks cache, fetches on miss, fills and returns; a hit is not a freshness guarantee.
Keys distinguish values, and application code owns cache-aside reads and writes.
Source commit and cache deletion are separate operations and cache-aside consistency is not guaranteed; old-fill race follows documented operations.
Redis distinguishes expiration from capacity eviction, allows eviction of TTL-bearing keys, and supports noeviction refusal.
Process-local copies may disagree; external caches share entries but add operations and availability risks.
AWS documents concurrent-miss overload, coalescing, limiting downstream requests or shedding, and testing with cache disabled.
Reuse, source cost, volatility and observed performance determine whether caching is beneficial.
